transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just feel like I’ve got a motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. 

Like at work, if we have a staff meeting, or when I'm sitting through briefings for church events. I just can't seem to stay put. I end up shifting around in my chair a lot, or standing up in the back, or I just have to find some excuse to get up and move around. It's getting pretty frustrating, honestly.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, particularly for mood or stomach issues?
No, I'm not taking any prescription medications. Um, nothing for my mood, and my stomach is fine, so I don't take anything for that either. I'm just not on any pills right now.
Has this feeling of needing to move around been something you have dealt with for most of your life, or is this a relatively new experience for you?

It's been most of my life, really. I mean, I remember getting in trouble way back in grade school because I was always popping out of my seat. I'd end up talking over the teacher, or... or I'd just rush ahead and start doing things before the directions were even finished. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a little kid. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me at all.
